source: Parke RL, Eccleston ML, McGuinness SP. The effects of flow on airway pressure during high-flow nasal therapy. Respir Care 2011; 56(8):1151-1155; Groves N, Tobin A. Aust Crit Care 2007; 20(4):126-131.
claim: High-flow nasal therapy with mouth open generates positive airway pressure of approximately 0.05 cmH2O per L/min flow (Parke 2011, Groves & Tobin 2007), yielding approximately 2.5 cmH2O of continuous airway distending pressure at 50 L/min.
